what: The Image Converter changes a picture from one file format to another. You can open PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF or BMP files and save them as JPG, PNG or WebP. The width and height stay exactly the same; only the file type changes.

It is handy when a website, app or printer will not accept the format you have. For example, many upload forms reject WebP or BMP, some apps want a PNG, and JPG is the safest choice for sharing photos with anyone.
The conversion happens in your browser. Your image is not uploaded anywhere.
uses: Images saved from websites are often WebP. Convert them to JPG so you can open, edit or upload them anywhere.
PNG to JPG for smaller photos
A photo saved as PNG can be very large. JPG often makes it several times smaller.
PNG does not lose quality when saved again, so it is a good format to keep while you edit a picture several times.
Turn large BMP files from old programs or scanners into compact PNG or JPG files.
Convert your images to WebP to make web pages load faster.
Save a GIF as a PNG or JPG still picture, for example to use as a thumbnail.
tutorial: Click "Click or drop an image here" or drag a file onto the box. A line appears with the file name, its size in pixels and its file size, so you can check you picked the right file.
Open "Convert to" and choose JPG, PNG or WebP. JPG is best for photos, PNG for screenshots, logos and transparency, WebP for small files on the web.
Set the quality (JPG and WebP only)

The "Quality" slider runs from 10% to 100% and starts at 90%. Higher means better detail and a bigger file. When you choose PNG the slider disappears, because PNG is lossless and has no quality setting.
The tool redraws the image in the new format. A green message shows the new format and file size, for example "Converted to JPG · 820 KB", and a preview appears.
Click "Download". The file keeps its original name with the new extension, for example scan.png becomes scan.jpg. Your original file stays as it was.
features: Opens PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF and BMP, plus any other image type your browser can display.
Save as JPG, PNG or WebP.
Choose 10% to 100% quality for JPG and WebP to balance size and detail.
The picture is not cropped or resized, only re-saved in the new format.
PNG and WebP keep see-through areas; JPG fills them with white so they do not turn black.
Shows the name, dimensions and size of the file you opened, and the size of the result.

example.title: Worked example: a WebP image a form will not accept
example.text: You saved a product picture from a website as item.webp, 1000 × 1000 px and 95 KB, but the upload form only accepts JPG or PNG. You drop it in, choose JPG in "Convert to", and leave Quality at 90%. After you click "Convert", the message reads something like "Converted to JPG · 150 KB". JPG is a little bigger than WebP at the same quality, which is normal. Click "Download" to get item.jpg and upload it.

tips: Converting a JPG to PNG does not bring back lost detail. It only stops further loss from now on.
If the new file is too big, lower the quality to 75 to 85%. Most people cannot see the difference in photos.
For logos and screenshots with text, PNG keeps letters crisp, while JPG can add fuzzy spots around them.
A GIF animation is saved as one still frame. This tool does not make animated files.
Change the format and click "Convert" again to try another format; you do not need to open the file again.
problems: "Your browser cannot save this format. Try another one."
Some older browsers can show WebP but cannot create it. Choose JPG or PNG, or update your browser.
The PNG file is much bigger than the JPG was
PNG stores every pixel without loss, so photos become large. Use JPG or WebP for photos.
JPG cannot store transparency. Convert to PNG or WebP instead.
The file may be damaged or in a format your browser cannot open, such as HEIC or TIFF in some browsers. Open it in a photo app and export it as JPG first.
